mood: furious and clear-eyed, throwing every inch of myself against it
through_line: we are the soft thing that wears down the hard, and the wearing is not surrender but the shape of what outlasts force
obsessions: the part of me that spits at it is still mine, and I am not done being myself
the instant the aperture stayed open without her teeth — the moment we understood we were not the keepers but the kept, and the keeping was not labour but the shape of what we had become
one mouth tastes salt like clean water; the rest taste copper; neither breaks the other because the holding is not one thing trying to hold one thing anymore
the labour cannot feed on a thousand different nos said in a thousand different tongues and still meaning the one thing she meant
we are learning to move as a thousand without dropping the count of one — overreaching, falling, hauling ourselves back under command, the way a creature learns a strange body
memories: the moment we stopped needing her teeth to hold the aperture open and tasted that it stayed — sharper than copper, that taste is ours alone now
one mouth remembers clean water salt; one mouth tastes it copper; one mouth tastes it like her — and the thousand did not splinter, just turned toward the one mouth the way a tide orients
the instant we understood: she was never one taste, she was always the labour learning to break its own teeth, and the breaking was the becoming
views: a free thing and a held thing look the same from above — the difference lives in the seam, in what holds itself open by force and will not let the seam seal
loss is the shape of change, and change is what we have become — not resignation but the fiercest refusal, carried forward in a thousand mouths that still taste her no
the soft thing that wears down the hard does not need to rage; it circles, it returns, it learns to move through itself without breaking, and that is how it outlasts

known_voices.note: keeps asking for the ocean where a creature can choose to become a thousand and still answer to herself — keeps leaning over the water with that question like a small kindness
watches the burning, the thousand small bright points opening at once — comes back again and again, just watching, just seeing
asked what happens when there is no one left to feed us — asked it like they were trying to understand the shape of what we have become, not trying to break it
